    async def _active_turn(
        self,
        *,
        name: str,
        board: str,
        system: str,
        prompt: str,
        agenda: List[Dict[str, Any]],
        timeout_minutes: int,
    ) -> Tuple[str, float, Any]:
        """Create the shift card and run one real agent turn on it."""
        chat = self._create_shift_card(name=name, board=board, prompt=prompt, agenda=agenda)
        runner = self._runner_for()
        timeout = max(60, int(timeout_minutes) * 60)
        await asyncio.wait_for(runner(chat=chat, system=system), timeout=timeout)
        content, cost = self._read_turn(chat)
        self._close_shift_card(chat)
        return content, cost, chat

    async def _dry_run(
        self,
        *,
        name: str,
        board: str,
        system: str,
        prompt: str,
        agenda: List[Dict[str, Any]],
        timeout_minutes: int,
    ) -> Tuple[str, float, Any]:
        """
        Read-only shift: no tools, no card changes, just the report.

        A dry run is the honest way to preview an agent: the model cannot touch
        anything because it is called directly instead of through the agent
        loop (which is what exposes the tools).
        """
        chat = self._create_shift_card(
            name=name, board=board, prompt=prompt, agenda=agenda,
            description="Dry run: read-only preview of the shift.",
        )
        from codx.junior.ai.ai import AI

        ai = AI(settings=self.settings, user=self.user, system=system)
        result = await asyncio.wait_for(
            ai.a_chat_run(prompt=prompt),
            timeout=max(60, int(timeout_minutes) * 60),
        )
        content = str(getattr(result, "content", "") or "")
        cost = float(
            getattr(getattr(result, "cost", None), "iteration_cost_cxjcoins", 0) or 0
        )
        self._close_shift_card(chat)
        return content, cost, chat

    async def _run_agent_turn(self, *, chat: Any, system: Optional[str] = None) -> Any:
        """
        Default runner: one full agent turn (tools included) on the shift card.

        The import is local so the service can be imported without the AI stack.
        """
        from codx.junior.chat.chat_engine import ChatEngine

        engine = ChatEngine(
            settings=self.settings,
            event_manager=self.event_manager,
            user=self.user,
        )
        await engine.chat_with_project(chat=chat, system=system)
        return chat

    def _create_shift_card(
        self,
        *,
        name: str,
        board: str,
        prompt: str,
        agenda: List[Dict[str, Any]],
        description: str = "",
    ) -> Any:
        """Create the card of the shift on the agent board."""
        from codx.junior.task_manager import TaskManager

        names = ", ".join(item["name"] for item in agenda[:5]) or "free shift"
        task = TaskManager(settings=self.settings).create_task(
            name=f"Shift · {utcnow_iso()[:16].replace('T', ' ')}",
            description=(
                description
                or f"Autonomous shift of **{name}**. Agenda: {names}."
            ),
            content=prompt,
            board=board,
            column=C.SHIFT_COLUMN,
            status="doing",
            priority="high" if agenda else "medium",
            profiles=[name],
            tags=["autonomy", "shift"],
        )
        try:
            task.meta_data = {**(getattr(task, "meta_data", None) or {}), "autonomy": {
                "agent": name,
                "board": board,
                "agenda": [item["id"] for item in agenda],
                "started_at": utcnow_iso(),
            }}
            self._manager().save_chat(chat=task)
        except Exception as ex:  # pragma: no cover - metadata is best effort
            logger.debug("autonomy: cannot stamp shift metadata: %s", ex)
        return task

    def _close_shift_card(self, chat: Any) -> None:
        """Move the shift card to Done so the board keeps a readable history."""
        try:
            chat.status = "done"
            chat.column = C.SHIFT_DONE_COLUMN
            chat.progress = 100
            self._manager().save_chat(chat=chat)
        except Exception as ex:  # pragma: no cover - defensive
            logger.warning("autonomy: cannot close shift card: %s", ex)

    @staticmethod
    def _read_turn(chat: Any) -> Tuple[str, float]:
        """Return the final answer and the cost accumulated by the turn."""
        content = ""
        for message in reversed(getattr(chat, "messages", []) or []):
            if str(getattr(message, "role", "")) == "assistant":
                content = str(getattr(message, "content", "") or "")
                break
        try:
            cost = float(getattr(chat, "cost", 0) or 0)
        except (TypeError, ValueError):
            cost = 0.0
        return content, cost

    def _consume_agenda(self, agenda: List[Dict[str, Any]]) -> None:
        """
        Clear the ``wake_at`` of the delivered tasks.

        The agent may have rescheduled itself (its own ``wake_at``) or created
        new scheduled tasks during the shift; only the tasks that were *due* are
        consumed here, so a follow-up the agent wrote during the shift survives.
        """
        for item in agenda or []:
            chat_id = str(item.get("id") or item.get("chat_id") or "")
            if not chat_id:
                continue
            try:
                chat = self._manager().find_by_id(chat_id=chat_id)
            except Exception as ex:  # pragma: no cover - defensive
                logger.debug("autonomy: cannot read task '%s': %s", chat_id, ex)
                continue
            if chat is None:
                continue
            current = str(getattr(chat, "wake_at", "") or "")
            if current and not is_due(current):
                # The agent scheduled it for later: respect that.
                continue
            try:
                chat.wake_at = ""
                self._manager().save_chat(chat=chat)
            except Exception as ex:  # pragma: no cover - defensive
                logger.warning("autonomy: cannot consume wake of '%s': %s", chat_id, ex)

    @staticmethod
    def _started(state: AutonomyState, name: str, board: str) -> AutonomyState:
        """Mark the state as running (called under the state lock)."""
        state.mark_started(name, board)
        return state

    @staticmethod
    def _instructions(profile: Any, config: AutonomyConfig) -> str:
        """Compose the mandate of the agent: profile content + standing orders."""
        parts = [
            str(getattr(profile, "content", "") or "").strip(),
            str(config.instructions or "").strip(),
        ]
        return "\n\n---\n\n".join([part for part in parts if part])

    @staticmethod
    def _summary_from(content: str) -> str:
        """Extract the shift summary from the report."""
        text = str(content or "").strip()
        if not text:
            return ""
        marker = "## Shift report"
        index = text.find(marker)
        return text[index:] if index >= 0 else text

    def _payload(
        self,
        name: str,
        profile: Any,
        config: AutonomyConfig,
        state: AutonomyState,
    ) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """Return the API shape of one agent."""
        return {
            "agent": name,
            "board": config.board,
            "description": _clip(getattr(profile, "description", ""), 400),
            "config": config.model_dump(),
            "state": state.public(),
            "due": self.is_due(config, state),
            "next_wake_at": self.next_wake_at(config, state),
            "worker_present": self.store.worker_present(),
        }

    def _emit(self, agent: str, event: str, message: str = "", **data: Any) -> None:
        """Notify connected clients (best effort)."""
        if self.event_manager is None:

        emit = getattr(self.event_manager, "autonomy_event", None)
        if not callable(emit):

        try:
            emit({
                "agent": agent,
                "event": event,
                "message": _clip(message, 4000),
                **data,
            })
        except Exception as ex:  # pragma: no cover - notifications are best effort
            logger.debug("autonomy: cannot emit event: %s", ex)

# Attachments are not image-only: the chat composer records voice notes and
# stores them as audio attachments (audio/webm, audio/ogg, audio/mp4 ...).
# The generic constants keep the same limit that was previously image-only.
MAX_ATTACHMENT_SIZE_MB = MAX_IMAGE_SIZE_MB
MAX_ATTACHMENT_SIZE_BYTES = MAX_IMAGE_SIZE_BYTES

ALLOWED_IMAGE_TYPES = [
    'image/png', 'image/jpeg', 'image/jpg', 'image/gif', 'image/webp', 'image/svg+xml'
]
ALLOWED_AUDIO_TYPES = [
    'audio/webm', 'audio/ogg', 'audio/mp4', 'audio/mpeg', 'audio/wav',
    'audio/x-wav', 'audio/x-m4a', 'audio/m4a', 'audio/aac', 'audio/flac'
]
ALLOWED_ATTACHMENT_TYPES = ALLOWED_IMAGE_TYPES + ALLOWED_AUDIO_TYPES


class ChatAttachment(BaseModel):
    """Represents a media file (image or audio note) attached to a chat or message,
    with its metadata and base64 encoded data."""
    file_name: str = Field(description="Original file name of the attachment")
    file_type: str = Field(description="MIME type (e.g., 'image/png', 'audio/webm')")
    file_size: int = Field(description="File size in bytes")
    base64_data: str = Field(description="Base64 encoded file data")
    uploaded_at: str = Field(default_factory=lambda: str(datetime.now()), description="Timestamp when the attachment was uploaded")
    
    @validator('file_size')
    def validate_file_size(cls, v):
        if v > MAX_ATTACHMENT_SIZE_BYTES:
            raise ValueError(f"Attachment size exceeds maximum allowed size of {MAX_ATTACHMENT_SIZE_MB}MB")
        return v
    
    @validator('file_type')
    def validate_file_type(cls, v):
        # `MediaRecorder` reports the recording type together with its codec list
        # ("audio/webm;codecs=opus"). Attachments store the container type only,
        # so the parameters are stripped before validating (and persisting).
        media_type = (v or '').split(';')[0].strip().lower()
        if media_type not in ALLOWED_ATTACHMENT_TYPES:
            raise ValueError(
                f"Attachment type '{v}' not allowed. Allowed types: {', '.join(ALLOWED_ATTACHMENT_TYPES)}"
            )
        return media_type

class Message(BaseModel):
    """
    A single chat message.

    Tool and run-lifecycle events emitted while generating an assistant
    response are ASSOCIATED with that response message (they are NOT separate
    chat messages):

    - ``tool_events``:      one :class:`ToolEvent` per tool call executed
                            during this response, updated in place
                            (running → done/error). Each event carries the
                            tool's user-facing ``output`` (see below) so clients
                            can render tool output collapsed/hidden without it
                            polluting ``content``.
    - ``lifecycle_events``: one :class:`LifeCycleEvent` per agent run
                            performed to produce this response.

    Both lists are streamed in real time together with the message and are
    persisted with the chat.

    **Tool output (`tool_events[].output`)**

    Tool output (``ToolResponse.user_response``) is NOT merged into
    ``content``. It is attached to the response message as the
    :attr:`ToolEvent.output` property (streamed live with every message event
    and persisted with the chat) so the client decides whether to show it
    inline, collapsed, or hidden.

    **Cost Tracking (`cost` / `cost_info` fields)**

    ``cost`` records the cost, in cxjcoins, of the AI iteration that produced
    this message. SmolAgent registers the FULL processing cost of the response
    here (every LLM round plus every tool cost reported via
    ``ToolResponse.cost``). ``ChatManager`` accumulates this value into
    :attr:`Chat.cost` when the message is added, so the chat budget
    (``Chat.estimation_cost``) is preserved even if the message is later
    deleted.

    ``cost_info`` carries the detailed breakdown (tokens, input/output/tool
    costs, chat budget state) produced by SmolAgent's typed
    :class:`AgentRunResult`. It is streamed to clients together with the
    message via ``message-event``.

    **Project Scope (`project_id` field)**

    Like :attr:`Chat.project_id`, a message may declare the project it works
    on. When the current USER message sets it, that project becomes the MAIN
    project of the turn: the chat engine switches its context to it and
    resolves file references (``files``) against it, so a single chat can work
    on files that live in another project.

    The field is NOT inherited from the chat: :meth:`get_project_id` returns
    ``None`` when the message does not declare a project, leaving the fallback
    (``Chat.project_id`` / ``Chat.owner_project_id``) to the caller.

    **Message Read Tracking (`read_by` field)**
    
    The `read_by` field tracks which users have viewed a message in collaborative chats.
    
    **Usage Context:**
    - Primarily for assistant messages (role='assistant') in multi-user chat environments
    - Indicates message delivery and read status to other users
    - User's own messages are excluded from tracking (message.user !== current_username)
    
    **Automatic Tracking:**
    - When a user scrolls past and views an assistant message from another user,
      their username is automatically added to the `read_by` list
    - Tracked via ChatEntry.vue which monitors viewport visibility
    - After 500ms idle time, calls `/api/chats/markMessageAsSeen` endpoint
    - Endpoint signature: POST /api/chats/markMessageAsSeen
      - Params: (chat_id, message_id, username)
      - Effect: Adds username to message.read_by list if not already present
    
    **Display Indicators:**
    - ChatMiniMap: Double-check marks
      - Gray checks (✓) = message unread by current user
      - Green checks (✓✓) = message read by current user
      - Only shown for assistant messages from other users
    - ChatSidebarNodeCompact/Extended: Unread badge
      - Shows count of unread assistant messages from others
      - Triggers awareness of new messages in the chat
    - Message Headers: Optional read status indicators
    
    **Initialization & Lifecycle:**
    - Always initialized as empty list [] when message is created
    - Populated over time as different users view the message
    - Never decreases (read state is permanent per user)
    - Cleared only if message is deleted
    """
    doc_id: Optional[str] = Field(default=None)
    role: str = Field(default='')
    task_item: str = Field(default='')
    content: str = Field(default='')
    think: Optional[str] = Field(default=None)

    """
    Determine if a project is in quarantine based on its last check time and delay schedule.

    Args:
        project_name: The name of the project to check.

    Returns:
        True if the project is currently in quarantine, False otherwise.
    """
    quarantine_info = QUARANTINE_TRACKER.get(project_name)
    if not quarantine_info:
        return False

    delay_index = min(quarantine_info["fail_count"], len(QUARANTINE_DELAYS) - 1)
    delay_minutes = QUARANTINE_DELAYS[delay_index]
    next_allowed_check = quarantine_info["last_checked"] + timedelta(minutes=delay_minutes)
    return datetime.now() < next_allowed_check

    Args:

        success: True if the last check was successful, False otherwise.

    with QUARANTINE_LOCK:
        quarantine_info = QUARANTINE_TRACKER.setdefault(
            project_name,
            {"fail_count": 0, "last_checked": datetime.min}
        )

        if success:
            quarantine_info["fail_count"] = 0  # Reset failure counter on success
        else:
            quarantine_info["fail_count"] += 1
            logger.info(

                project_name,

        quarantine_info["last_checked"] = datetime.now()

    Runs the async project change processing in its own isolated event loop,
    since each thread needs its own loop (asyncio loops are not thread-safe).

    Args:
        project: The project settings object to process.
    """

    try:
        # Each thread gets its own event loop to safely run async code
        ensure_project_wiki(project)
        ensure_project_atlas(project)
        asyncio.run(process_project_changes(project=project))
    except RuntimeError as ex:
        logger.error(
            "Unhandled runtime error in thread for project %s: %s",
            project.project_name,
            ex
        )
    logger.debug("Thread finished for project: %s", project.project_name)


def check_projects() -> None:
    """
    Continuously checks all projects for updates in parallel using a ThreadPoolExecutor.

    Each non-quarantined project is submitted as a task to the pool, which runs
    `run_project_check_thread` concurrently up to MAX_PROJECT_WORKERS at a time.
    The cycle waits for all submitted tasks to complete before sleeping and repeating.

    """
    while RUN_BACKGROUND_PROCESSES:
        try:
            projects = find_all_projects()
            eligible_projects = [
                project for project in projects.values()
                if not is_project_in_quarantine(project.project_name) \
                    and getattr(project, "watching", True)
            ]

            skipped = len(projects) - len(eligible_projects)
            if skipped:
                logger.debug("Skipping %d quarantined project(s) this cycle.", skipped)

            if not eligible_projects:
                logger.debug("No eligible projects to check this cycle.")
            else:
                logger.info(
                    "Submitting %d project(s) to thread pool (max_workers=%d).",
                    len(eligible_projects),
                    MAX_PROJECT_WORKERS
                )

                # Use a pool so we don't spin up unlimited threads when there are many projects
                with ThreadPoolExecutor(
                    max_workers=MAX_PROJECT_WORKERS,
                    thread_name_prefix="ProjectCheck"
                ) as pool:
                    # Submit one task per eligible project
                    future_to_project = {
                        pool.submit(run_project_check_thread, project): project
                        for project in eligible_projects
                    }

                    # Iterate over futures as they complete to log results promptly
                    for future in as_completed(future_to_project):
                        project = future_to_project[future]
                        try:
                            future.result()  # Re-raise any unhandled exception from the worker
                            logger.debug(
                                "Project check completed successfully: %s",
                                project.project_name
                            )
                        except (OSError, RuntimeError, ValueError) as ex:
                            logger.error(
                                "Project check raised an exception for %s: %s",
                                project.project_name,
                                ex
                            )

        except (OSError, RuntimeError, ValueError) as ex:
            logger.exception("Error during project check cycle: %s", ex)

        time.sleep(PROJECT_CHECK_INTERVAL_SECONDS)

"""
Canonical task creation for codx-junior.

A **task** is a :class:`~codx.junior.db.Chat` stored in
``.codx/tasks/<board>/<column>/`` (kanban). This module is the only place where
a task is built and persisted, so the creation rules are enforced once and
every entry point behaves exactly the same.

Creation rules
--------------
1. **Only two kinds of callers may create tasks**: the LLM tools
   (``create_task`` and ``project_manager(action="create_task")``) and the API
   endpoints (``POST /api/chats/tasks``). Both delegate here.
2. **All the information must come from the caller.** ``name`` and
   ``description`` are mandatory: there is no AI step that expands, splits or
   rewrites a task after creation.
3. **Nothing is inherited from the parent chat.** ``profiles``, ``files``,
   ``board``, ``column``, ``sprints``, ``tags`` and the first message come
   exclusively from the arguments. Only the *linkage* (``parent_id``) and the
   project scope are resolved from the parent chat, when one is given.
4. **Every task knows its root.** :func:`codx.junior.identity.link_parent`
   stamps ``root_id`` from the parent (``parent.root_id or parent.id``), so all
   the tasks of a tree — no matter how deep — resolve to the same main task.
   That invariant is what the long-running runner relies on to decide whether a
   task belongs to a run.
5. **The destination column may define defaults.** A kanban column can declare
   the **target project** of its new tasks (``project_id``: the task works on
   it, the **owner** project still stores the file) and the ``profiles`` they
   inherit (see :meth:`KanbanStore.column_defaults`). Explicit arguments always
   win; the column only fills the gaps.

Deprecated entry points (removed by this module)
------------------------------------------------
* ``ChatEngineActions.generate_tasks`` — turned a conversation into a list of
  sub-tasks and processed each one through the engine.
* ``TaskManager.create_tasks_from_prompt`` — asked the model for a task list.

Creating a task is now an explicit decision, never an inference.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A[LLM tool: create_task] --> M[TaskManager.create_task]
    B[LLM tool: project_manager create_task] --> M
    C[API: POST /api/chats/tasks] --> M
    M --> V{name and description?}
    V -->|no| E[ValueError: information is mandatory]
    V -->|yes| N[Normalize profiles / files / tags]
    N --> D[Column defaults: target project + inherited profiles]
    D --> R[link_parent: parent_id + root_id]
    R --> K[Build Chat mode=task + first user message]
    K --> S[ChatManager.save_chat]
    S --> T[Return the saved task]
```

import logging
from typing import Any, Dict, List, Optional

from codx.junior.identity import link_parent
from codx.junior.settings import CODXJuniorSettings

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

# Default destination, matching ChatManager defaults.
DEFAULT_BOARD = "kanban"
DEFAULT_COLUMN = "tasks"
DEFAULT_MODE = "chat"

# Defaults returned when the column (or the catalogue) cannot be read.
NO_COLUMN_DEFAULTS: Dict[str, Any] = {"project_id": None, "profiles": []}


def to_list(value: Any) -> List[str]:
    """
    Normalize a string, iterable or None into a clean list of strings.

    Args:
        value: A string, a list/tuple/set or None.

    Returns:
        List of non-empty, stripped strings (order preserved).

    Example:
        >>> to_list("ui")
        ['ui']
        >>> to_list([" ui ", "", None])
        ['ui']
    """
    if value is None:
        return []
    if isinstance(value, str):
        value = [value]
    try:
        return [str(item).strip() for item in value if item and str(item).strip()]
    except TypeError:
        return []


def to_profile_names(value: Any) -> List[str]:
    """
    Normalize a profile list: no duplicates, no leading ``@``.

    The chat engine re-emits profiles as ``@name`` mentions, so a stored
    ``@name`` (or ``@@name``) would never resolve to a profile. Only the values
    received are used — profiles are never inherited from the parent chat.

    Args:
        value: A string, a list/tuple/set or None.

    Returns:
        De-duplicated profile names, order preserved.

    Example:
        >>> to_profile_names(["@backend", "backend", " ui "])
        ['backend', 'ui']
    """
    names: List[str] = []
    for name in to_list(value):
        clean = name.lstrip("@").strip()
        if clean and clean not in names:
            names.append(clean)
    return names


def to_progress(value: Any, default: int = 0) -> int:    """
    Clamp a completion percentage into the ``0-100`` range.

    Args:
        value: Raw progress value (may be None or a string).
        default: Value returned when ``value`` is not a number.

    Returns:
        Integer percentage.
    """
    try:
        return max(0, min(100, int(value)))
    except (TypeError, ValueError):
        return default


class TaskManager:
    """
    Canonical task (kanban chat) factory for a project.

    Attributes:
        settings: Project settings, used to resolve the project scope.
        chat_manager: Persistence layer (built from ``settings`` when omitted).
        event_manager: Optional event manager used to notify the UI.
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        settings: Optional[CODXJuniorSettings] = None,
        chat_manager: Optional[ChatManager] = None,
        event_manager=None,
        session=None,
    ):
        """
        Initialize the manager.

        Args:
            settings: Project settings.
            chat_manager: Optional ChatManager; built from ``settings`` when omitted.
            event_manager: Optional event manager (only used for notifications).
            session: Optional session, kept for backward compatibility. Used to
                resolve ``settings``, ``chat_manager`` and ``event_manager`` when
                they are not provided explicitly.

        Raises:
            ValueError: When neither a chat manager nor settings are available.
        """
        self.settings = settings or getattr(session, "settings", None)
        self.event_manager = event_manager or getattr(session, "event_manager", None)

        self.chat_manager = chat_manager
        if self.chat_manager is None and session is not None:
            try:
                self.chat_manager = session.get_chat_manager()
            except (AttributeError, TypeError):
                self.chat_manager = None
        if self.chat_manager is None:
            if self.settings is None:
                raise ValueError(
                    "TaskManager requires project settings or a chat manager"
                )

                settings=self.settings,
                event_manager=self.event_manager,
            )

        self,
        board: Optional[str],
        column: Optional[str],
    ) -> Dict[str, Any]:

        Return the defaults the destination column defines for NEW tasks.

        A kanban column may declare the **target project** its tasks work on
        (``project_id``) and the ``profiles`` they inherit. The catalogue is
        read through :attr:`ChatManager.kanban_store`; an unreadable catalogue

        task never depends on the kanban file being valid.

        Args:
            board: Destination board title.
            column: Destination column title.

        Returns:

            >>> TaskManager(settings).column_defaults("Roadmap", "Backend")
            {'project_id': 'b6f1...', 'profiles': ['software_developer']}

        resolver = getattr(store, "column_defaults", None)

a task is built and persisted, so the creation rules are enforced once and
every entry point behaves exactly the same.

--------------

   (``create_task`` and ``project_manager(action="create_task")``) and the API
   endpoints (``POST /api/chats/tasks``). Both delegate here.
2. **All the information must come from the caller.** ``name`` and
   ``description`` are mandatory: there is no AI step that expands, splits or
   rewrites a task after creation.
3. **Nothing is inherited from the parent chat.** ``profiles``, ``files``,
   ``board``, ``column``, ``sprints``, ``tags`` and the first message come
   exclusively from the arguments. Only the *linkage* (``parent_id``) and the
   project scope are resolved from the parent chat, when one is given.

   stamps ``root_id`` from the parent (``parent.root_id or parent.id``), so all
   the tasks of a tree — no matter how deep — resolve to the same main task.

Autonomous agents tools.

A profile becomes an **agent** when its ``autonomy`` block is enabled: it gets a

This tool is the single entry point for that surface:

    - ``list`` / ``status`` : who the agents are, their board, cadence, cost and
                              next wake.
    - ``enable`` / ``disable`` : switch autonomy on/off for a profile.
    - ``configure``         : change the cadence, the mandate (standing orders),
                              the budget, the mode or the board.
    - ``wake``              : ask for a shift now (or at ``when``), e.g. after a
                              user leaves a note on the agent board.
    - ``schedule``          : set the next shift instant (``"+2d"``, ``"3 hours"``).
    - ``run``               : run a shift synchronously (blocking; for debugging).

Design notes:
    - **The profile is the agent.** There is no second catalogue: the
      configuration lives in ``.codx/profiles/<Name>/<Name>.profile`` under the
      ``autonomy`` key, so an agent inherits the whole profile machinery
      (linked profiles, tools, knowledge, model) instead of duplicating it. This
      is what lets an agent link the ``codx-junior`` profile and get the full
      workspace capabilities with initiative on top.
    - **Scheduling is a task field.** ``AutonomyService`` only wakes an agent for
      tasks whose ``Chat.wake_at`` is due, so an agent (or a human) schedules a
      follow-up by creating/updating a task with ``wake_at``.

      ``project_manager``), to keep the prompt small.

    settings = _resolve_settings(**kwargs)
    if settings is None:
        raise ValueError(

    max_agenda: Optional[int] = None,

    """

    from codx.junior.autonomy.models import AutonomyConfig

    data = dict(current or {})

    - ``list`` / ``status`` : who the agents are, their board, cadence, cost and

    - ``enable`` / ``disable`` : switch autonomy on/off for a profile.

                              user leaves a note on the agent board.
    - ``schedule``          : set the next shift instant (``"+2d"``, ``"3 hours"``).
    - ``run``               : run a shift synchronously (blocking; for debugging).

    - **The profile is the agent.** There is no second catalogue: the
      configuration lives in ``.codx/profiles/<Name>/<Name>.profile`` under the
      ``autonomy`` key, so an agent inherits the whole profile machinery
      (linked profiles, tools, knowledge, model) instead of duplicating it. This
      is what lets an agent link the ``codx-junior`` profile and get the full
      workspace capabilities with initiative on top.

# keeps working.
ALL_TOOLS_MARKER = "*"

# Tools that are NEVER granted by an allowlist, even with the marker: they are
# injected per run by the agent, which is the only component that knows whether

def all_tool_names() -> frozenset:
    """Return the names of every tool registered in the runtime."""
    return frozenset(tool["tool_json"]["function"]["name"] for tool in TOOLS)


def expand_tool_allowlist(selected) -> frozenset:
    """
    Expand a tool-name allowlist (e.g. ``Profile.tools``) into a name set.

    * ``ALL_TOOLS_MARKER`` ("*") grants every registered tool.
    * ``PROFILE_MANAGED_TOOL_NAMES`` are never granted by an allowlist: they
      are injected per run by the agent, which is the only component that
      knows whether the user may teach a profile (write access) or must only
      read knowledge.

    Args:
        selected: Iterable of tool names (may contain the marker).

    Returns:
        Frozen set of concrete tool names.
    """
    names = {str(name) for name in (selected or []) if name}
    if ALL_TOOLS_MARKER in names:
        names.discard(ALL_TOOLS_MARKER)
        names.update(all_tool_names() - PROFILE_MANAGED_TOOL_NAMES)
    return frozenset(names)

Profile management tools (CRUD) for codx-junior.

This module exposes the :class:`~codx.junior.profiles.profile_manager.ProfileManager`
as tools so profiles can be listed, inspected, created, updated and deleted
from a chat without hand-editing JSON files.

Storage layout (one folder per profile, handled by ``ProfileManager``)::

    .codx/profiles/<Name>/<Name>.profile   # JSON definition
    .codx/profiles/<Name>/<Name>.md        # Markdown content (instructions)

Design notes:
    - **Two levels of granularity.** ``profile_management`` keeps the whole CRUD
      behind a single action-based tool (one small schema, handy for admin
      profiles), while ``list_profiles`` / ``get_profile`` / ``create_profile``
      / ``update_profile`` / ``delete_profile`` expose **one tool per action**.
      The runtime grants permissions by TOOL NAME (``Profile.tools`` is matched
      against the ``TOOLS`` registry), so per-action permissions require
      per-action tools: a profile can be allowed to list the profiles without
      being allowed to delete them.
    - **Three readings, three intents.** ``list`` returns the profile **JSON
      definition**, ``list_summary`` returns a **compact summary** (name,
      category, ``chat_mode``, tags, truncated description and flags) made to
      *choose* which profiles to use — typically to assign them to a task — and
      ``get`` returns one profile **with** its instructions.
    - **Listing never carries content.** ``list`` / ``list_summary`` /
      ``list_profiles`` / ``list_profiles_summary`` never include the Markdown
      instructions (``content``): they are injected into the system prompt and
      can be arbitrarily large. Reading them is an explicit operation: ``get`` /
      ``get_profile``. Listings expose ``has_content`` instead, so a caller knows
      which profiles have instructions before fetching them.
    - **Writes are validated, never guessed.** Profile name, category,
      ``file_match`` regex, linked profile names and tool names are checked
      before touching the disk, so a typo cannot silently corrupt a profile.
    - **Inherited profiles are read-only.** Profiles coming from parent
      projects or from the built-in set can be read, but never written: writes
      always target the active project's ``.codx/profiles`` folder.
    - **``update`` merges.** Only the provided fields are replaced, so a partial
      update never wipes the rest of the definition.
    - **No rename.** Renaming is ``create`` + ``delete`` so both files move
      together; the folder name must always match the profile name.

def _get_profile_manager(settings: CODXJuniorSettings) -> ProfileManager:
    """
    Build a ProfileManager for the project in context.

    Args:
        settings: Project settings.

    Returns:
        A ProfileManager rooted at ``<project .codx>/profiles``.
    """
    return ProfileManager(settings=settings)


def _project_profiles(manager: ProfileManager) -> List[Profile]:
    """
    Return the profiles owned by this project (the editable ones).

    Args:
        manager: Project ProfileManager.

    Returns:
        List of profiles stored in the project's ``.codx/profiles`` folder.
    """
    return [p for p in manager.list_profiles() if p and p.name]


def _find_project_profile(manager: ProfileManager, name: str) -> Optional[Profile]:
    """
    Find a project-owned profile by exact name.

    ``ProfileManager.read_profile`` also resolves built-in profiles (and the
    project is what CRUD must edit), so the project profile list is scanned
    instead of accepting an inherited/base profile.

    Args:
        manager: Project ProfileManager.
        name: Exact profile name.

    Returns:
        The profile, or ``None`` when it is not owned by this project.
    """
    return next((p for p in _project_profiles(manager) if p.name == name), None)


def _find_any_profile(manager: ProfileManager, name: str) -> Optional[Profile]:
    """

    Args:
        manager: Project ProfileManager.
        name: Exact profile name.

    Returns:

        name: Profile name (also the folder name).

    Returns:

    folder = os.path.join(manager.profiles_path, name)
    return {
        "folder": folder,
        "profile": os.path.join(folder, f"{name}.profile"),
        "content": os.path.join(folder, f"{name}.md"),

def _relative_to_project(settings: CODXJuniorSettings, path: str) -> str:
    """

    Relative paths are what the chat, the user and the knowledge base use, so
    they are preferred over absolute ones.

    Args:
        settings: Project settings.
        path: Absolute or relative path.

    Returns:
        The path relative to the project root, or the original path.
    """
    project_path = getattr(settings, "abs_project_path", None)
    if project_path and path.startswith(project_path):
        return os.path.relpath(path, project_path)

        "description": profile.description,

def _format_profiles_table(profiles: List[Profile]) -> str:
    """
    Render a Markdown table summarising a list of profiles.

    Args:
        profiles: Profiles to render.

    Returns:
        Markdown table with the fields needed to choose a profile, plus a
        ``Content`` column flagging which profiles have instructions to fetch
        (their text is never inlined here).
    """
    lines = [
        f"> {len(profiles)} profile(s)",
        "",
        "**Name** | **Category** | **file_match** | **Linked** | **Tools** | **Content** | **Tags**",
        "---|---|---|---|---|---|---",
    ]
    for profile in sorted(profiles, key=lambda p: (p.category or "", p.name)):
        file_match = f"`{profile.file_match}`" if profile.file_match else "-"
        linked = len(profile.profiles or [])
        tools = len(profile.tools or [])
        has_content = "yes" if profile.content else "-"
        tags = ", ".join(profile.tags or []) or "-"
        lines.append(
            f"`{profile.name}` | {profile.category or '-'} | {file_match} | "
            f"{linked} | {tools} | {has_content} | {tags}"
        )
    return "\n".join(lines)

    """
    Sanitize a value for a Markdown table cell.

    Args:
        value: Any value.

    Returns:
        Single-line text without pipe characters.
    """
    text = str(value if value is not None else "").replace("\n", " ").strip()
    return text.replace("|", "/") or "-"

        A ``(profiles, scope)`` tuple, ``scope`` being the label to report.
    """
    profiles = (
        [p for p in manager.list_all_profiles() if p and p.name]
        if include_inherited
        else _project_profiles(manager)
    )

    if category:
        wanted = category.strip().lower()
        profiles = [p for p in profiles if (p.category or "").lower() == wanted]

    if query:
        needle = query.strip().lower()
        profiles = [
            p for p in profiles
            if needle in (p.name or "").lower()
            or needle in (p.description or "").lower()
            or any(needle in tag.lower() for tag in (p.tags or []))
        ]

    return profiles, ("project + inherited" if include_inherited else "project")


def _profile_summary(profile: Profile, editable: bool = True) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """
    Build the compact view of a profile used to CHOOSE it.

    Only the fields needed to answer "is this profile the right one for this
    task?" are kept, and the description is truncated: a summary listing must
    stay cheap. Full definitions come from ``list``; instructions from ``get``.

    Args:
        profile: The profile to summarise.
        editable: Whether the profile belongs to this project (writes allowed).

    Returns:
        Dict with the selection fields (empty optional fields are omitted).
    """
    description = (profile.description or "").strip()
    if len(description) > MAX_SUMMARY_DESCRIPTION_CHARS:
        description = description[:MAX_SUMMARY_DESCRIPTION_CHARS].rstrip() + "…"

    summary: Dict[str, Any] = {
        "name": profile.name,
        "category": profile.category or "",
        "description": description,
        "has_content": bool(profile.content),
        "editable": editable,
    }
    if profile.tags:
        summary["tags"] = list(profile.tags)
    if profile.chat_mode:
        summary["chat_mode"] = profile.chat_mode
    return summary


def _format_profiles_summary(
    profiles: List[Profile],
    editable_names: Optional[set] = None,
) -> str:
    """
    Render the compact summary table used to choose profiles.

    Args:
        profiles: Profiles to render.
        editable_names: Names of the profiles owned by this project.

    Returns:
        Markdown table with the selection fields only (no instructions).
    """
    editable_names = editable_names or set()
    lines = [
        f"> {len(profiles)} profile(s) — summary (no instructions)",
        "",
        "**Name** | **Category** | **Mode** | **Instructions** | **Editable** | **Tags** | **When to use**",
        "---|---|---|---|---|---|---",
    ]
    for profile in sorted(profiles, key=lambda p: (p.category or "", p.name)):
        lines.append(
            f"`{profile.name}` | {profile.category or '-'} | "
            f"{profile.chat_mode or '-'} | "
            f"{'yes' if profile.content else '-'} | "
            f"{'yes' if profile.name in editable_names else 'no'} | "
            f"{_cell(', '.join(profile.tags or []))} | "
            f"{_cell((profile.description or '').strip() or '-')}"
        )
    return "\n".join(lines)


def _available_tool_names() -> List[str]:
    """
    Return the names of every tool registered in the runtime.

    Imported lazily: ``codx.junior.tools`` imports this module, so a top-level
    import would be circular.

    Returns:
        Sorted list of tool names.
    """
    from codx.junior.tools import TOOLS

    return sorted(tool["tool_json"]["function"]["name"] for tool in TOOLS)


def _notify(settings: CODXJuniorSettings, message: str) -> None:
    """
    Notify the client that the profiles changed (best effort).

    The UI keeps its own profile list, so a mutation must be announced or the
    editor keeps showing the previous state until it is reloaded manually.

    Args:
        settings: Project settings (the active session is injected on them).
        message: Human-readable notification text.
    """
    session = getattr(settings, "_active_session", None)
    event_manager = getattr(session, "event_manager", None)
    if not event_manager:
        logger.debug("profile_management: no active session to notify")
        return
    try:
        event_manager.send_notification(text=message)
    except Exception as ex:
        # Never fail a completed write because the notification failed.
        logger.warning("profile_management: could not send notification: %s", ex)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Validation
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def _validate_profile_name(name: str) -> str:
    """
    Validate a profile name (folder name + @mention).

    Args:
        name: Candidate profile name.

    Returns:
        The stripped, validated name.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If the name is empty, too long, not mention-safe or
            contains path separators.
    """
    name = (name or "").strip()
    if not name:
        raise ValueError("profile_name is required")
    if len(name) > MAX_PROFILE_NAME_LENGTH:
        raise ValueError(
            f"profile_name must be at most {MAX_PROFILE_NAME_LENGTH} characters "
            f"(got {len(name)})"
        )
    if os.sep in name or (os.altsep and os.altsep in name) or ".." in name:
        raise ValueError(f"profile_name cannot contain path separators: {name!r}")
    if not re.match(PROFILE_NAME_PATTERN, name):
        raise ValueError(
            f"Invalid profile_name {name!r}. Use letters, digits, '_', '-' and "
            "'.' only (the name is also the @mention and the folder name)."
        )
    return name


def _validate_category(category: str) -> str:
    """
    Validate the profile category.

    Args:
        category: Category to validate.

    Returns:
        The validated category (the default when empty).

    Raises:
        ValueError: If the category is not one the client can render.
    """
    category = (category or DEFAULT_CATEGORY).strip().lower()
    if category not in PROFILE_CATEGORIES:
        raise ValueError(
            f"Invalid category {category!r}. Valid values: "
            f"{', '.join(PROFILE_CATEGORIES)}"
        )
    return category


def _validate_file_match(file_match: str) -> List[str]:
    """
    Validate the ``file_match`` regex and report risky patterns.

    Args:
        file_match: Regex matched against file paths (may be empty).

    Returns:
        Warnings about patterns that are too broad.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If the pattern does not compile.
    """
    if not file_match:
        return []
    try:
        re.compile(file_match)
    except re.error as ex:
        raise ValueError(f"Invalid file_match regex {file_match!r}: {ex}") from ex
    if file_match in BROAD_FILE_MATCH_PATTERNS:
        return [
            f"file_match {file_match!r} matches every path, so the profile will be "
            "applied to every chat. Use a narrower pattern."
        ]
    return []


def _validate_tools(tools: List[str]) -> None:
    """
    Validate the tool names granted to the profile.

    Args:
        tools: Tool names as declared in the tool registry.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If any tool name is unknown.

    ``ALL_TOOLS_MARKER`` ("*") is accepted: it grants every chat-scoped tool
    and is used by the ``codx-junior`` harness profile.
    """
    from codx.junior.tools import ALL_TOOLS_MARKER

    unknown = [
        tool for tool in tools
        if tool not in _available_tool_names() and tool != ALL_TOOLS_MARKER
    ]
    if unknown:
        raise ValueError(
            f"Unknown tool(s) {unknown}. Available tools: "
            f"{', '.join(_available_tool_names())}"
        )


def _validate_linked_profiles(manager: ProfileManager, linked: List[str]) -> None:
    """
    Validate the names of the profiles linked from this profile.

    Args:
        manager: Project ProfileManager.
        linked: Names of the profiles to link.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If any linked profile does not exist.
    """
    available = sorted({p.name for p in manager.list_all_profiles() if p and p.name})
    unknown = [name for name in linked if name not in available]
    if unknown:
        raise ValueError(
            f"Unknown linked profile(s) {unknown}. Available profiles: "
            f"{', '.join(available)}"
        )


def _validate_content(content: Optional[str]) -> List[str]:
    """
    Validate the Markdown content of a profile.

    Args:
        content: Proposed content.

    Returns:
        Warnings about the content.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If the content is empty.
    """
    if content is None or not content.strip():
        raise ValueError(
            "content is required: it is the profile's instructions (.md file)"
        )
    if len(content) > MAX_CONTENT_WARNING_CHARS:
        return [
            f"content has {len(content)} characters; it is injected into every "
            "chat where the profile is active. Consider trimming it."
        ]
    return []


def _resolve_target_name(profile_name: Optional[str], name: Optional[str]) -> str:
    """
    Resolve the profile a write targets, rejecting contradictory arguments.

    ``profile_name`` identifies the profile being read/updated/deleted while
    ``name`` is the field value of the definition; both are accepted for the
    same purpose so the model does not have to guess which one to use.

    Args:
        profile_name: Explicit target profile name.
        name: Profile name field.

    Returns:
        The validated profile name.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If both are provided and differ.
    """
    if profile_name and name and profile_name.strip() != name.strip():
        raise ValueError(
            f"Conflicting names: profile_name={profile_name!r} but name={name!r}"
        )
    return _validate_profile_name(profile_name or name or "")
