request.content:
"""
Team generation from a plain-language need.

A manager says *"I need an IT team"* or *"someone to take care of the
maintenance tickets"* — not a profile list. This module turns that sentence into
a **proposal** and, when asked, into real profiles + a team.

Two steps, deliberately separated so the UI can preview before writing anything:

* :func:`suggest` — pure proposal. It reuses
  :func:`codx.junior.company.profile_advisor.recommend`, which inspects the
  project stack and maps the need onto known roles, and enriches it with the
  **actor block** each new profile would get (so an autonomous team can be
  generated with a weekly availability window in one shot).
* :func:`apply` — writes the profiles that are missing, then the team and its
  charter. It never overwrites an existing profile: a role whose profile already
  exists is reused as-is (its actor block is not touched, that is the user's
  decision).

The team is written with :class:`~codx.junior.teams.team_manager.TeamManager`, so
the folder layout (``.codx/teams/<Name>/<Name>.team`` + ``.md``) and the
``@mention`` behaviour are exactly the same as when a team is created by hand:
the generator is a shortcut for the manual flow, not a second one.

Made with ❤️ by codx-junior
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import logging
import re
from typing import Any, Dict, List, Optional

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

#: Profile names are folder names and @mentions: keep them boring.
_NAME_RE = re.compile(r"^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_.-]*$")


def _valid_name(name: str) -> bool:
    """Return True when *name* can be used as a profile name (and a folder)."""
    return bool(
        name
        and len(name) <= 64
        and ".." not in name
        and "/" not in name
        and "\\" not in name
        and _NAME_RE.match(name)
    )


def _available_profiles(settings: Any) -> List[str]:
    """Return the profile names visible from the project (best effort)."""
    try:
        from codx.junior.profiles.profile_manager import ProfileManager

        return [
            str(getattr(profile, "name", "") or "")
            for profile in ProfileManager(settings=settings).list_all_profiles() or []
            if getattr(profile, "name", None)
        ]
    except Exception as ex:  # pragma: no cover - catalogue is best effort
        logger.warning("team generator: cannot list profiles: %s", ex)
        return []


def _projects(settings: Any) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
    """Return the project in the shape the advisor expects."""
    project_id = str(getattr(settings, "project_id", "") or "")
    project_name = str(getattr(settings, "project_name", "") or "")
    project_path = str(getattr(settings, "project_path", "") or "")
    if not project_id and not project_path:
        return []
    return [{
        "project_id": project_id or project_name,
        "project_name": project_name or project_id,
        "project_path": project_path,
    }]


def _actor_block(
    role: Dict[str, Any],
    *,
    autonomous: bool,
    board: str,
    schedule: Optional[Dict[str, Any]],
) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """
    Return the ``actor`` block of a generated profile.

    A generated teammate is a **coworker** by default: it owns its job, works
    until it is done or the budget is over, and writes its shift reports on its
    own desk board. The schedule is copied as-is so a generated team can be kept
    inside office hours from the start.
    """
    if not autonomous:
        return {}
    from codx.junior.autonomy import constants as C
    from codx.junior.autonomy.models import ActorConfig, default_board_name

    name = str(role.get("profile_name") or "")
    watched = [board] if board else []
    desk = default_board_name(name)
    return ActorConfig(
        enabled=True,
        role=C.ROLE_COWORKER,
        policy=C.POLICY_FULL,
        session=C.SESSION_UNTIL_DONE,
        board=desk,
        boards=watched,
        interval_minutes=24 * 60,
        daily_budget_cxjcoins=0.0,
        instructions=(
            f"You own the \"{role.get('title')}\" responsibility of this team. "
            "Work until the job is done or the daily budget is over, and "
            "schedule every follow-up as a task with `wake_at`."
        ),
        schedule=schedule or {},
    ).normalized().model_dump()


def suggest(
    settings: Any,
    need: str,
    *,
    autonomous: bool = False,
    board: str = "",
    schedule: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None,
) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """
    Turn a plain-language need into a team proposal.

    Args:
        settings: Project settings.
        need: What the user asked for ("I need an IT team", "take care of the
            maintenance tickets", ...).
        autonomous: When True every generated profile also gets an ``actor``
            block, so the team works on its own.
        board: Board the generated actors are responsible for. Empty leaves each
            actor on its own desk board.
        schedule: Weekly availability applied to the generated actors.

    Returns:
        The advisor suggestion, enriched with ``actor`` (the block that would be
        written) on every role and the derived team members.
    """
    from codx.junior.company.profile_advisor import recommend

    project_name = str(getattr(settings, "project_name", "") or "")
    suggestion = recommend(
        need,
        company_name=project_name,
        available_profiles=_available_profiles(settings),
        available_tools=None,
        projects=_projects(settings),
    )
    roles = suggestion.get("roles") or []
    for index, role in enumerate(roles):
        role["order"] = index
        role["actor"] = _actor_block(
            role, autonomous=autonomous, board=board, schedule=schedule
        )
    suggestion["autonomous"] = bool(autonomous)
    suggestion["board"] = board
    suggestion["schedule"] = schedule or {}
    suggestion["members"] = [
        {
            "profile": role.get("profile_name"),
            "role": "lead" if index == 0 else role.get("role_id"),
            "responsibility": role.get("description") or "",
            "order": index,
        }
        for index, role in enumerate(roles)
        if role.get("profile_name")
    ]
    return suggestion


def _charter(
    name: str,
    suggestion: Dict[str, Any],
    members: List[Dict[str, Any]],
) -> str:
    """
    Build the markdown charter of a generated team.

    Kept close to the charter the ``team_management`` tool generates for a hand
    written team, plus the two things that only exist when the team is
    autonomous: the shift report habit and the availability window.
    """
    lines = [f"# {name} team", ""]
    goal = str(suggestion.get("need") or "").strip()
    if goal:
        lines.extend([f"**Goal:** {goal}", ""])
    lines.extend(["## How we work"])
    lead = members[0]["profile"] if members else ""
    if lead:
        lines.append(
            f"1. **@{lead}** coordinates: splits the request, assigns it to the "
            "members below and consolidates the final answer."
        )
    lines.append("2. Each member works only inside its responsibility.")
    lines.append(
        "3. Conflicts are resolved explicitly; a decision is never silent."
    )
    if suggestion.get("autonomous"):
        lines.append(
            "4. Every member works its own board and leaves a shift report, so "
            "the progress of the team can be read without asking."
        )
        lines.append(
            "5. Anything that must be checked later becomes a task with "
            "`wake_at`. An unscheduled follow-up is a lost follow-up."
        )
    lines.append("")
    if members:
        lines.extend(["## Responsibilities", ""])
        for member in members:
            role = f" ({member['role']})" if member.get("role") else ""
            responsibility = (
                f" — {member['responsibility']}" if member.get("responsibility") else ""
            )
            lines.append(f"- **@{member['profile']}**{role}{responsibility}")
        lines.append("")
    return "\n".join(lines)


def apply(
    settings: Any,
    suggestion: Dict[str, Any],
    *,
    team_name: str = "",
) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """
    Write the profiles and the team of *suggestion*.

    Args:
        settings: Project settings.
        suggestion: The payload returned by :func:`suggest`.
        team_name: Optional override of the generated team name.

    Returns:
        ``{"team": <team dict or empty>, "created_profiles": [...],
        "reused_profiles": [...], "errors": [...]}``

    Existing profiles are never modified: a role that already has a profile is
    reused as-is.
    """
    from codx.junior.model.profile import Profile, ProfileApiSettings
    from codx.junior.model.team import Team
    from codx.junior.profiles.profile_manager import ProfileManager
    from codx.junior.teams.team_manager import TeamManager

    profiles_manager = ProfileManager(settings=settings)
    team_manager = TeamManager(settings=settings)
    project_name = str(getattr(settings, "project_name", "") or "")
    project_id = str(getattr(settings, "project_id", "") or "")
    stack = suggestion.get("stack") or {}

    # The suggestion may come back from the client between two requests, so the
    # names are validated here again before anything is written to disk.
    available = {
        str(name).lower(): str(name) for name in _available_profiles(settings)
    }

    created: List[str] = []
    reused: List[str] = []
    errors: List[str] = []
    members: List[Dict[str, Any]] = []

    for index, role in enumerate(suggestion.get("roles") or []):
        name = str(role.get("profile_name") or "").strip()
        if not _valid_name(name):
            errors.append(f"invalid profile name {name!r}")
            continue
        existing = available.get(name.lower())
        if existing:
            reused.append(existing)
            members.append({
                "profile": existing,
                "role": "lead" if index == 0 else str(role.get("role_id") or "member"),
                "responsibility": str(role.get("description") or "")[:200],
                "order": len(members),
            })
            continue
        if not role.get("create"):
            errors.append(
                f"{name}: the profile does not exist and was not requested"
            )
            continue
        try:
            from codx.junior.company.profile_advisor import profile_content

            profile = Profile(
                name=name,
                description=str(role.get("description") or "")[:400],
                category=str(role.get("category") or "agent"),
                content=profile_content(
                    role,
                    company_name=project_name,
                    project_name=project_name,
                    stack=stack,
                ),
                profiles=[str(base) for base in role.get("bases") or []],
                tools=[str(tool) for tool in role.get("tools") or []],
                tags=["generated", "team"],
                use_knowledge=True,
                api_settings=ProfileApiSettings(),
                actor=role.get("actor") or None,
                project_id=project_id,
            )
            profiles_manager.save_profile(profile=profile)
            available[name.lower()] = name
            created.append(name)
            members.append({
                "profile": name,
                "role": "lead" if index == 0 else str(role.get("role_id") or "member"),
                "responsibility": str(role.get("description") or "")[:200],
                "order": len(members),
            })
        except Exception as ex:  # pragma: no cover - per-profile isolation
            logger.exception("team generator: cannot create profile '%s': %s", name, ex)
            errors.append(f"{name}: {ex}")

    if not members:
        return {"team": {}, "created_profiles": created,
                "reused_profiles": reused, "errors": errors}

    resolved_name = str(team_name or suggestion.get("team_name") or "Team").strip()
    if not _valid_name(resolved_name):
        errors.append(f"invalid team name {resolved_name!r}")
        return {"team": {}, "created_profiles": created,
                "reused_profiles": reused, "errors": errors}
    if team_manager.read_team(resolved_name) is not None:
        return {
            "team": {},
            "created_profiles": created,
            "reused_profiles": reused,
            "errors": errors,
            "note": f"the team '{resolved_name}' already exists and was not modified",
        }

    try:
        team = Team(
            name=resolved_name,
            description=(
                f"Team generated for: {suggestion.get('need') or 'an expressed need'}"
            )[:400],
            goal=str(suggestion.get("need") or ""),
            lead=members[0]["profile"],
            members=members,
            tags=["generated"],
            project_id=project_id,
        )
        team.ensure_lead_in_roster()
        team.content = _charter(resolved_name, suggestion, members)
        saved = team_manager.save_team(team)
    except Exception as ex:  # pragma: no cover - defensive
        logger.exception("team generator: cannot create team: %s", ex)
        errors.append(f"team: {ex}")
        return {"team": {}, "created_profiles": created,
                "reused_profiles": reused, "errors": errors}

    return {
        "team": team_manager.resolve_team(saved),
        "created_profiles": created,
        "reused_profiles": reused,
        "errors": errors,
    }

    can read, edit and write it back without a partial-update dialect.

    Args:

        request: The incoming HTTP request.

    Returns:
        The persisted team definition (charter included).

    Raises:
        HTTPException: 400 when the body name differs from the path, 404 when
            the team does not exist.

    manager = get_team_manager(request)

    existing = manager.read_team(team_name)
    if not existing:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail=f"Team '{team_name}' not found")

    if team.name and team.name != team_name:
        raise HTTPException(
            status_code=400,
            detail=(
                f"Body team name '{team.name}' does not match the path "
                f"'{team_name}'. Renaming is POST + DELETE."
            ),
        )

    team.name = team_name
    team.project_id = existing.project_id or manager.settings.project_id
    team.created_at = existing.created_at
    team.ensure_lead_in_roster()

    saved = manager.save_team(team)
    logger.info("update_team: '%s'", saved.name)
    return saved.definition(include_content=True)

def delete_team(team_name: str, request: Request) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """
    Delete a team (its folder and both files).

    The profiles the team referenced are untouched: a team never owned them.

    Args:
        team_name: Exact name of the team to delete.

    Returns:

    manager = get_team_manager(request)

    existing = manager.read_team(team_name)

    members = existing.profile_names
    manager.delete_team(team_name)

    return {"deleted": team_name, "members": members}

# Dynamically set CODX_JUNIOR_PATH to the parent directory of the script

echo "CODX_JUNIOR_PATH: $CODX_JUNIOR_PATH"
echo "Starting api USER: ${USER} ($(id -u):$(id -g)) HOME: ${HOME}"

# source tree it must not touch: the recursive chown and `uv sync` below are
# installation steps, not start-up steps, and cost tens of seconds per restart.
# Set CODX_JUNIOR_SKIP_INSTALL=1 to skip them.
if [ "$CODX_JUNIOR_SKIP_INSTALL" != "1" ]; then
  echo "Fix permissions"
  sudo chown -R ${USER} ${HOME}
  sudo chown ${USER} /var/run/docker.sock 2>/dev/null || true
fi

source ${CODX_JUNIOR_PATH}/set_env.sh

export PYTHONPATH=${CODX_JUNIOR_PATH}/api

cd ${CODX_JUNIOR_PATH}/api

  echo "!!! venv not found. Installing at: ${CODX_JUNIOR_API_VENV}"

else
  echo "venv found!"
fi

source ${CODX_JUNIOR_API_VENV}/bin/activate

if [ "$CODX_JUNIOR_SKIP_INSTALL" != "1" ]; then
  # Sync the environment with pyproject.toml / uv.lock on start (development and
  # source-mounted deployments only: it downloads packages).
  uv sync
fi

if [ "$CODX_JUNIOR_API_BACKGROUND" != "" ]; then
  API_PORT=$CODX_JUNIOR_API_PORT_BACKGROUND

if [ "$DEBUG" == "" ]; then

fi

```py .codx/worktrees/autonomous-profiles/api/codx/junior/teams/generator.py
"""
Team generation from a plain-language need.

A manager says *"I need an IT team"* or *"someone to take care of the
maintenance tickets"* — not a profile list. This module turns that sentence into
a **proposal** and, when asked, into real profiles + a team.

Two steps, deliberately separated so the UI can preview before writing anything:

* :func:`suggest` — pure proposal. It reuses
  :func:`codx.junior.company.profile_advisor.recommend`, which inspects the
  project stack and maps the need onto known roles, and enriches it with the
  **actor block** each new profile would get (so an autonomous team can be
  generated with a weekly availability window in one shot).
* :func:`apply` — writes the profiles that are missing, then the team and its
  charter. It never overwrites an existing profile: a role whose profile already
  exists is reused as-is (its actor block is not touched, that is the user's
  decision).

The team is written with :class:`~codx.junior.teams.team_manager.TeamManager`, so
the folder layout (``.codx/teams/<Name>/<Name>.team`` + ``.md``) and the
``@mention`` behaviour are exactly the same as when a team is created by hand:
the generator is a shortcut for the manual flow, not a second one.

Made with ❤️ by codx-junior
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import logging
import re
from typing import Any, Dict, List, Optional

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

#: Profile names are folder names and @mentions: keep them boring.
_NAME_RE = re.compile(r"^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_.-]*$")


def _valid_name(name: str) -> bool:
    """Return True when *name* can be used as a profile name (and a folder)."""
    return bool(
        name
        and len(name) <= 64
        and ".." not in name
        and "/" not in name
        and "\\" not in name
        and _NAME_RE.match(name)
    )


def _available_profiles(settings: Any) -> List[str]:
    """Return the profile names visible from the project (best effort)."""
    try:
        from codx.junior.profiles.profile_manager import ProfileManager

        return [
            str(getattr(profile, "name", "") or "")
            for profile in ProfileManager(settings=settings).list_all_profiles() or []
            if getattr(profile, "name", None)
        ]
    except Exception as ex:  # pragma: no cover - catalogue is best effort
        logger.warning("team generator: cannot list profiles: %s", ex)
        return []


def _projects(settings: Any) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
    """Return the project in the shape the advisor expects."""
    project_id = str(getattr(settings, "project_id", "") or "")
    project_name = str(getattr(settings, "project_name", "") or "")
    project_path = str(getattr(settings, "project_path", "") or "")
    if not project_id and not project_path:
        return []
    return [{
        "project_id": project_id or project_name,
        "project_name": project_name or project_id,
        "project_path": project_path,
    }]


def _actor_block(
    role: Dict[str, Any],
    *,
    autonomous: bool,
    board: str,
    schedule: Optional[Dict[str, Any]],
) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """
    Return the ``actor`` block of a generated profile.

    A generated teammate is a **coworker** by default: it owns its job, works
    until it is done or the budget is over, and writes its shift reports on its
    own desk board. The schedule is copied as-is so a generated team can be kept
    inside office hours from the start.
    """
    if not autonomous:
        return {}
    from codx.junior.autonomy import constants as C
    from codx.junior.autonomy.models import ActorConfig, default_board_name

    name = str(role.get("profile_name") or "")
    watched = [board] if board else []
    desk = default_board_name(name)
    return ActorConfig(
        enabled=True,
        role=C.ROLE_COWORKER,
        policy=C.POLICY_FULL,
        session=C.SESSION_UNTIL_DONE,
        board=desk,
        boards=watched,
        interval_minutes=24 * 60,
        daily_budget_cxjcoins=0.0,
        instructions=(
            f"You own the \"{role.get('title')}\" responsibility of this team. "
            "Work until the job is done or the daily budget is over, and "
            "schedule every follow-up as a task with `wake_at`."
        ),
        schedule=schedule or {},
    ).normalized().model_dump()


def suggest(
    settings: Any,
    need: str,
    *,
    autonomous: bool = False,
    board: str = "",
    schedule: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None,
) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """
    Turn a plain-language need into a team proposal.

    Args:
        settings: Project settings.
        need: What the user asked for ("I need an IT team", "take care of the
            maintenance tickets", ...).
        autonomous: When True every generated profile also gets an ``actor``
            block, so the team works on its own.
        board: Board the generated actors are responsible for. Empty leaves each
            actor on its own desk board.
        schedule: Weekly availability applied to the generated actors.

    Returns:
        The advisor suggestion, enriched with ``actor`` (the block that would be
        written) on every role and the derived team members.
    """
    from codx.junior.company.profile_advisor import recommend

    project_name = str(getattr(settings, "project_name", "") or "")
    suggestion = recommend(
        need,
        company_name=project_name,
        available_profiles=_available_profiles(settings),
        available_tools=None,
        projects=_projects(settings),
    )
    roles = suggestion.get("roles") or []
    for index, role in enumerate(roles):
        role["order"] = index
        role["actor"] = _actor_block(
            role, autonomous=autonomous, board=board, schedule=schedule
        )
    suggestion["autonomous"] = bool(autonomous)
    suggestion["board"] = board
    suggestion["schedule"] = schedule or {}
    suggestion["members"] = [
        {
            "profile": role.get("profile_name"),
            "role": "lead" if index == 0 else role.get("role_id"),
            "responsibility": role.get("description") or "",
            "order": index,
        }
        for index, role in enumerate(roles)
        if role.get("profile_name")
    ]
    return suggestion


def _charter(
    name: str,
    suggestion: Dict[str, Any],
    members: List[Dict[str, Any]],
) -> str:
    """
    Build the markdown charter of a generated team.

    Kept close to the charter the ``team_management`` tool generates for a hand
    written team, plus the two things that only exist when the team is
    autonomous: the shift report habit and the availability window.
    """
    lines = [f"# {name} team", ""]
    goal = str(suggestion.get("need") or "").strip()
    if goal:
        lines.extend([f"**Goal:** {goal}", ""])
    lines.extend(["## How we work"])
    lead = members[0]["profile"] if members else ""
    if lead:
        lines.append(
            f"1. **@{lead}** coordinates: splits the request, assigns it to the "
            "members below and consolidates the final answer."
        )
    lines.append("2. Each member works only inside its responsibility.")
    lines.append(
        "3. Conflicts are resolved explicitly; a decision is never silent."
    )
    if suggestion.get("autonomous"):
        lines.append(
            "4. Every member works its own board and leaves a shift report, so "
            "the progress of the team can be read without asking."
        )
        lines.append(
            "5. Anything that must be checked later becomes a task with "
            "`wake_at`. An unscheduled follow-up is a lost follow-up."
        )
    lines.append("")
    if members:
        lines.extend(["## Responsibilities", ""])
        for member in members:
            role = f" ({member['role']})" if member.get("role") else ""
            responsibility = (
                f" — {member['responsibility']}" if member.get("responsibility") else ""
            )
            lines.append(f"- **@{member['profile']}**{role}{responsibility}")
        lines.append("")
    return "\n".join(lines)


def apply(
    settings: Any,
    suggestion: Dict[str, Any],
    *,
    team_name: str = "",
) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """
    Write the profiles and the team of *suggestion*.

    Args:
        settings: Project settings.
        suggestion: The payload returned by :func:`suggest`.
        team_name: Optional override of the generated team name.

    Returns:
        ``{"team": <team dict or empty>, "created_profiles": [...],
        "reused_profiles": [...], "errors": [...]}``

    Existing profiles are never modified: a role that already has a profile is
    reused as-is.
    """
    from codx.junior.model.profile import Profile, ProfileApiSettings
    from codx.junior.model.team import Team
    from codx.junior.profiles.profile_manager import ProfileManager
    from codx.junior.teams.team_manager import TeamManager

    profiles_manager = ProfileManager(settings=settings)
    team_manager = TeamManager(settings=settings)
    project_name = str(getattr(settings, "project_name", "") or "")
    project_id = str(getattr(settings, "project_id", "") or "")
    stack = suggestion.get("stack") or {}

    # The suggestion may come back from the client between two requests, so the
    # names are validated here again before anything is written to disk.
    available = {
        str(name).lower(): str(name) for name in _available_profiles(settings)
    }

    created: List[str] = []
    reused: List[str] = []
    errors: List[str] = []
    members: List[Dict[str, Any]] = []

    for index, role in enumerate(suggestion.get("roles") or []):
        name = str(role.get("profile_name") or "").strip()
        if not _valid_name(name):
            errors.append(f"invalid profile name {name!r}")
            continue
        existing = available.get(name.lower())
        if existing:
            reused.append(existing)
            members.append({
                "profile": existing,
                "role": "lead" if index == 0 else str(role.get("role_id") or "member"),
                "responsibility": str(role.get("description") or "")[:200],
                "order": len(members),
            })
            continue
        if not role.get("create"):
            errors.append(
                f"{name}: the profile does not exist and was not requested"
            )
            continue
        try:
            from codx.junior.company.profile_advisor import profile_content

            profile = Profile(
                name=name,
                description=str(role.get("description") or "")[:400],
                category=str(role.get("category") or "agent"),
                content=profile_content(
                    role,
                    company_name=project_name,
                    project_name=project_name,
                    stack=stack,
                ),
                profiles=[str(base) for base in role.get("bases") or []],
                tools=[str(tool) for tool in role.get("tools") or []],
                tags=["generated", "team"],
                use_knowledge=True,
                api_settings=ProfileApiSettings(),
                actor=role.get("actor") or None,
                project_id=project_id,
            )
            profiles_manager.save_profile(profile=profile)
            available[name.lower()] = name
            created.append(name)
            members.append({
                "profile": name,
                "role": "lead" if index == 0 else str(role.get("role_id") or "member"),
                "responsibility": str(role.get("description") or "")[:200],
                "order": len(members),
            })
        except Exception as ex:  # pragma: no cover - per-profile isolation
            logger.exception("team generator: cannot create profile '%s': %s", name, ex)
            errors.append(f"{name}: {ex}")

    if not members:
        return {"team": {}, "created_profiles": created,
                "reused_profiles": reused, "errors": errors}

    resolved_name = str(team_name or suggestion.get("team_name") or "Team").strip()
    if not _valid_name(resolved_name):
        errors.append(f"invalid team name {resolved_name!r}")
        return {"team": {}, "created_profiles": created,
                "reused_profiles": reused, "errors": errors}
    if team_manager.read_team(resolved_name) is not None:
        return {
            "team": {},
            "created_profiles": created,
            "reused_profiles": reused,
            "errors": errors,
            "note": f"the team '{resolved_name}' already exists and was not modified",
        }

    try:
        team = Team(
            name=resolved_name,
            description=(
                f"Team generated for: {suggestion.get('need') or 'an expressed need'}"
            )[:400],
            goal=str(suggestion.get("need") or ""),
            lead=members[0]["profile"],
            members=Team.parse_members(members),
            tags=["generated"],
            project_id=project_id,
        )
        team.ensure_lead_in_roster()
        team.content = _charter(resolved_name, suggestion, members)
        saved = team_manager.save_team(team)
    except Exception as ex:  # pragma: no cover - defensive
        logger.exception("team generator: cannot create team: %s", ex)
        errors.append(f"team: {ex}")
        return {"team": {}, "created_profiles": created,
                "reused_profiles": reused, "errors": errors}

    return {
        "team": team_manager.resolve_team(saved),
        "created_profiles": created,
        "reused_profiles": reused,
        "errors": errors,
    }
```

# Autonomous agents (actors)

An **actor** is a profile with initiative. It is a normal profile — same instructions, same
tools, same knowledge, same model — plus a declaration that tells codx-junior **when** it works,
**where** it works and **how much** it may spend.

Use actors for the jobs nobody wants to remember:

* take care of the maintenance tickets of the week;
* keep the agenda of a team in order;
* check a dependency, a certificate or a deployment again in two days;
* review a board every morning and report.

::: tip One runtime, two roles
There is no separate "board manager" feature any more. A **manager** that curates a board and a
**coworker** that owns a job are the same actor with a different role, tool policy and session
shape (see [Roles](#roles-manager-and-coworker)).
:::

## Declare an actor

The declaration lives **inside the profile** (`.codx/profiles/<Name>/<Name>.profile`), so it is
versioned with everything else the profile carries and it is reviewed like any other change.

```json
{
  "name": "ciso",
  "description": "Takes care of the security posture of the project.",
  "actor": {
    "enabled": true,
    "role": "coworker",
    "policy": "full",
    "session": "until_done",
    "boards": ["Security"],
    "board": "Agent: CISO",
    "interval_minutes": 1440,
    "daily_budget_cxjcoins": 20,
    "budget_cxjcoins": 5,
    "max_turns": 6,
    "max_agenda": 10,
    "instructions": "Focus on dependencies with known CVEs and on exposed secrets.",
    "schedule": {
      "enabled": true,
      "timezone": "Europe/Madrid",
      "windows": [{ "days": ["mon", "tue", "wed", "thu", "fri"], "start": "09:00", "end": "18:00" }]
    }
  }
}
```

| Field | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `enabled` | Turns the profile into an actor. |
| `role` | `coworker` (owns a job end to end) or `manager` (curates the boards it is responsible for). |
| `policy` | `full` (every tool of the profile) or `board_only` (boards and tasks only, never code). |
| `session` | `single` (one turn per shift) or `until_done` (keeps turning while work remains, bounded by `max_turns`). |
| `boards` | Boards the actor is **responsible for**: their tasks are its agenda. |
| `board` | **Desk** board where the shift reports are written. Defaults to the first watched board, or `Agent: <name>` (created on demand). |
| `interval_minutes` | Fallback cadence when nothing is scheduled (5 minutes – 30 days). |
| `mode` | `active` executes the tools, `dry_run` only reports what it *would* do. |
| `budget_cxjcoins` | Cap for one shift (`0` = project/chat default). |
| `daily_budget_cxjcoins` | Cap for one day across shifts (`0` = no cap). This is what makes "work until the job is done" safe. |
| `max_runtime_minutes` | Hard limit of one shift (default 30, maximum 180). |
| `max_turns` | Upper bound of turns inside an `until_done` shift. |
| `max_agenda` / `max_tasks` | How many due tasks the shift must handle / how many board tasks are given as context. |
| `include_done` | Whether closed tasks are also included as context. |
| `instructions` | Standing orders: the mandate of the actor, appended to the profile instructions. |
| `wake_at` | Next planned shift (ISO instant or an expression such as `+2d`). Empty derives it from the cadence. |
| `notify` | Comment the shift report on the desk board. |
| `schedule` | Weekly availability window (see [Quiet hours](#quiet-hours-a-weekly-schedule)). |

The same declaration can be written from a chat:

> Enable the actor for the profile `ciso`, let it work weekdays from 09:00 to 18:00 in
> Europe/Madrid, five cxjcoins per shift and twenty per day, and focus it on CVEs.

Becomes `autonomy_management(action="configure", profile_name="ciso", ...)`; the tool also
accepts `enable`, `disable`, `wake`, `schedule`, `run`, `status` and `list`.

## A shift

A **shift** is one bounded unit of autonomous work:

1. the runtime builds the agenda — the tasks of the actor boards whose `wake_at` is due;
2. it creates a **shift card** on the desk board and runs the first turn on it;
3. with `session: "until_done"` it keeps turning while work remains, until the agenda is empty,
   the per-shift budget, the daily budget or the clock runs out;
4. it writes the report on the shift card and moves it to `Done`;
5. it consumes the `wake_at` of the tasks it handled (a task the actor rescheduled for later
   during the shift keeps its new wake), and records the cost.

The desk board is created on first wake with four columns:

| Column | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `Inbox` | Work that arrived without a schedule. |
| `Scheduled` | Tasks with a future `wake_at`. |
| `Working` | The card of the shift in progress. |
| `Done` | Finished shifts and tasks. |

If the process dies mid-shift the card stays in `Working`; after `STALE_SHIFT_SECONDS` (15
minutes) the next shift may run, so a crash never blocks an actor forever.

## Scheduling: `wake_at`

`wake_at` is the alarm clock of a task (a *deadline* is `due_date`). Any task can carry one, and
the actor responsible for its board is woken when it becomes due:

```python
project_manager(action="create_task", name="Check the TLS certificate",
                description="Renew it if it expires before the next check.",
                board="Security", column="Scheduled", wake_at="+2d")
```

Accepted expressions are relative (`+2d`, `6 hours`, `2 weeks`, `in 90m`), a date (`2026-04-03`,
that day at 00:00 UTC) or an ISO instant. `project_manager(action="update_task", wake_at="")`
clears it.

This is the mechanism behind "an actor decides by itself what to do next": the prompt requires
every follow-up to be written as a task with `wake_at`, because an unscheduled follow-up is a
lost follow-up.

## Quiet hours: a weekly schedule

Actors are powerful and can be wrong. A schedule is how a team keeps them out of the hours where
**nobody is online to review their work**.

* `enabled: false` (default) means always available — what an agent needs to catch up after a
  downtime.
* When enabled, a shift only starts inside a window; a due task that falls outside is **kept**
  (its `wake_at` is not consumed) and handled at the next opening. `next_opening()` is what the
  UI shows as "next wake".
* `end <= start` is an **overnight** window (`22:00`–`06:00` is the night shift, owned by the
  listed days).
* Windows are read in `timezone` (IANA name, `Europe/Madrid`), never in server time.
* An **enabled schedule without windows** means *paused*.
* A **manual** wake (`POST /actors/{name}/wake`) always wins over the schedule: it is an explicit
  human decision.

An operator who needs everything to run right now can bypass the windows globally with
`CODX_JUNIOR_ACTORS_SCHEDULE=false`.

## Roles: manager and coworker

| | `role: "manager"` | `role: "coworker"` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Sees the board as | the queue it **curates** | its **desk** |
| Tool policy | `board_only` | `full` |
| Session | `single` (one review) | `until_done` |
| Typical use | review the status of the tasks, request information, reorganise the board | own a job ("CISO", "maintenance"), work until done or budget out |

The role only changes the prompt; the policy changes the tool set; the session changes how many
turns a shift may take. Everything else — worker, lock, state, ledger, schedule — is shared.

A board that still carries the legacy `board.manager` block keeps working: it is translated into
an actor on load (`BoardManagerConfig.to_actor_config`), with the reviewed board as its subject
and its own desk board for the reports.

## Generate a team from a need

Writing five profiles by hand to get a team is the wrong entry point. **Team View → Generate**
(and the company assistant) accept a sentence:

> I need someone to take care of the maintenance tickets, only during office hours.

Two steps, so nothing is written blindly:

1. `POST /api/teams/generate/suggest` returns a **proposal**: the roles the project advisor mapped
   from the need, which of them already exist, and the `actor` block each new profile would get
   (role, session, desk board, availability window);
2. `POST /api/teams/generate/apply` writes the missing profiles, then the team and its charter.

Existing profiles are **never modified** by the generator: a role whose profile already exists is
reused as-is, and its actor block stays exactly the way you configured it.

## Guardrails

* **Dry run first.** `mode: "dry_run"` gives you the reports without a single write.
* **Budget per shift and per day.** `budget_cxjcoins` caps one shift, `daily_budget_cxjcoins` caps
  the day across shifts (the day is UTC). The project budget still applies.
* **Time.** `max_runtime_minutes` stops a shift that runs away; `max_turns` bounds an
  `until_done` session.
* **One shift at a time.** Every actor takes a `flock` derived from its name, so two workers (API
  and background process, or a restart overlap) never run the same actor at once. This matters
  because an actor has write access to the repository.
* **Policy.** `board_only` restricts an actor to boards and tasks — a structural guarantee, not a
  post-hoc filter.
* **Environment switches.** `CODX_JUNIOR_ACTORS=0` disables the feature,
  `CODX_JUNIOR_ACTORS_WORKER=0` keeps the API but stops the background worker,
  `CODX_JUNIOR_ACTORS_SCHEDULE=false` ignores every availability window,
  `CODX_JUNIOR_ACTORS_TICK_SECONDS` and `CODX_JUNIOR_ACTORS_MAX_AGENTS` tune the loop.
  (The older `CODX_JUNIOR_AUTONOMY*` names are still read.)

## API

The router is mounted under `/api/actors` (`/api/autonomy` is kept as a hidden alias):

| Endpoint | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /actors/status` | Every actor: configuration, state, schedule, due flag, next wake, daily spend. |
| `GET /actors` | Only the actors. |
| `GET /actors/boards` | Boards that can be watched (title, id, columns). |
| `PUT /actors/{profile}` | Partial update of the actor block (upsert; the rest of the profile is untouched). |
| `POST /actors/{profile}/enable`, `/disable` | Toggle the actor. |
| `POST /actors/{profile}/wake?when=+2d` | Request a shift (queued; the worker runs it). |
| `POST /actors/{profile}/schedule?when=+2d` | Set the next planned shift. |
| `POST /actors/{profile}/run` | Run one shift now (blocking, for tests and debugging). |

The API process never runs a shift inline: it reads state and writes the "take a shift" intent.
The background worker (started with the other background services) finds the actors that are due
and runs their shifts, a few at a time.

Connected clients receive live updates on the `codx-junior-actors` channel (`started`, `finished`,
`error`, `wake`, `scheduled`, `skipped`).

## Cost and accountability

Every shift produces exactly one card, so the history of an actor is readable on its board: what
it saw, what it did, what it cost and why it stopped (`single`, `done`, `turns`, `budget`,
`daily_budget`, `runtime`, `schedule`). The per-actor state (`.codx/actors/state.json`) keeps the
same ledger in machine-readable form — shifts, last status, last stop reason, total cost, daily
cost — which is the raw material for scoring and rewarding the actors later on.
